newsitem.title: USA: Power Lenders seek New York securitization changes.
newsitem.headline: Power Lenders seek New York securitization changes.

text.p: Major lenders to New York utilities and independent power producers believe the securitization proposal pending before the state legislature could be improved.

In testimony presented to the Senate Energy Committee Wednesday, the National Power Lenders Forum said it is concerned by "the severe limit (the proposed legislation places) on the kinds of costs that could qualify for securitization."
It cited the proposed limiting of secuitization to expenditures that do not result in acquisition of property.
But Carrier Corp suggested to the committee that "we believe the intent of this legislation is to limit securitization to intangible assets only.

Speaking for the United Technologies Corp subsidiary, manager of government affairs Susan M. Crossett suggested "these intangible assets be limited to renegotiated or the buyout of independent power producer contracts, and regulatory assets."
Other power users called for "limiting the utilities' assets which qualify for such financing to those for which traditional securitized financing has not been available."

Barbara Brenner, speaking for the Industrial Energy Consumers Coalition, said the group recommends "limiting the assets subject to securitization to regulatory assets and above-market independent power contracts.
"The other asets owned by Utilities are not 'intangible,' and, therefore, it seems to us, can obtain traditional financing," she said.

The power lenders forum describes itself as an association of 25 domestic and international financial institutions with substantial loans and investments in independent power facilities and electric utilities.

It said "the state will realize the maximum benefit from securitization if all approved stranded costs qualify for securitization, including the above-market portion of IPP contracts, the above-market portion of utility-owned generating assets and any 'regulatory assets,' i.e. bookkeeping entries stemming from previous regulatory commitments."

The forum also said the act should be amended to set legislative guidelines on issues in the transition to electric competition rather than leaving these issues solely up the the Public Service Commission.

These changes should "narrow the delegation of authority" to the commission, saying it is given "overly broad authority to fix and adjust terms relating to the financing, refinancing and assignment of special intangible property".

The group also questioned provisions that would authorize regulators "to determine that 'portions of the qualified intangibles expenditures shall not be recoverable at all'," saying they "have the effect of increasing, rather than decreasing, stranded costs.

"These provisions appear to raise constitutional issues and could interfere with utility rights under preemptive federal laws. As a results, they will inevitably bog down the securitization program in costly and disruptive litigation."

Utilities operating in New York Statek include Central Hudson Gas and Electric Corp, Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, Orange and Rockland Utilities Inc, New York State Electric & Gas Corp, Long Island Lighting Co, Rochester Gas & Electric Corp and Niagara Mohawk Power Corp.
